gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that the Anker SOLIX S5000 does not work with Anker's Home Power Panel, so it reaches house circuits only through a transfer switch or inlet box on its L14-30R, and that Anker says its 120 V and 240 V outputs cannot be used at the same time.
standout_why: Compared against OffGrid Current's whole-home page (cited), The Solar Lab's big-stations page (cited) and the powerstations.reviews database (cited). OffGrid Current already has part of it: for the S5000, 'Only Anker's matching batteries fit', five expansion batteries to about 30 kWh, and both solar voltage windows; for the Jackery, the Smart Transfer Switch, a 240 V manual transfer switch and five Battery Pack 5000 Plus; for the TITAN 5000 Classic, Smart Home Panel 10 and no 240 V output. It has no home-connection, generator or outlet-exclusion line for the S5000, and makes the 'outlets don't run at the same time' point only for the DELTA Pro 3. The Solar Lab page covers only the Jackery in this class and names no accessory model. powerstations.reviews has no compatibility data for this group. Popular Mechanics and Car and Driver (both cited) are blocked to my fetcher, so I could not check them. Popular Mechanics is a full S5000 review and may carry some of this, which is why this is not a 3.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's split rather than changing it: the S5000 is the essentials unit. Its maker-documented house hookup is a manual 10-circuit transfer switch or inlet box on the 240 V L14-30R, capped at the station's 4,500 W, with no Anker automatic panel and no use of the 120 V outlets alongside the 240 V one. A shopper who wants automatic panel switchover has to look at the Jackery 5000 Plus or an EcoFlow TITAN, and I could not open either maker's page today to confirm those pairings. Separately, Anker's page says orders placed on or after Nov 25 ship within 15-16 weeks, so under the four-week rule the S5000 cannot be the pick if any other 5 kWh unit ships sooner.

findings.label: Home panel compatibility (maker FAQ)
findings.value: Not compatible with Anker SOLIX Home Power Panel; connect to the home electrical panel via a compatible transfer switch or power inlet box
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station (UL9540 and UL9540A Certified)
findings.note: FAQ verbatim: 'No. Anker SOLIX S5000 is not compatible with Anker SOLIX Home Power Panel. For essential circuit backup, connect it to your home electrical panel via a compatible transfer switch or power inlet box.' This URL (found by search) rendered the S5000 product page itself, with the H1 given as source_title; the canonical product URL was not shown.

findings.label: 120 V and 240 V outputs together (maker FAQ)
findings.value: Cannot be used simultaneously; per-port maximums are NEMA 5-20R 2,400 W, TT-30R 3,600 W, 240 V L14-30R 4,500 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station (UL9540 and UL9540A Certified)
findings.note: FAQ 'What is the maximum AC output power for each port when using a 120V or 240V input?' ends: 'Please note: 120V and 240V outputs cannot be used simultaneously.' Anker does not elaborate in the text I read. Arithmetic: 4,500 W / 240 V = 18.75 A, so the station, not a 30 A cable (7,200 W at 240 V), is the limit on the L14-30R.

findings.label: Expansion battery pairing and exclusions (maker FAQ)
findings.value: BP5000 only; BP3800, BP3000 and third-party batteries are not supported
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station (UL9540 and UL9540A Certified)
findings.note: FAQ 'Is Anker SOLIX S5000 compatible with third-party batteries or previous models like BP3800 or BP3000?' Answer: 'No. Anker SOLIX S5000 supports only BP5000 expansion batteries.' Anker's /s5000 page shows configurations up to 'S5000 + 5× Batteries (30kWh)'.

findings.label: Expansion batteries and Smart Generator together (maker FAQ)
findings.value: Supported; the generator connects to the second DC port on the expansion battery, or the DC port on the topmost battery in a stack
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station (UL9540 and UL9540A Certified)
findings.note: The second sentence of the FAQ answer was truncated in my read; check the full wording before quoting it.

findings.label: Price and dispatch notice
findings.value: $2,499.99 (list $3,599.99); 'Orders placed on or after November 25th will ship within 15 - 16 weeks.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station (UL9540 and UL9540A Certified)
findings.note: Read on Anker's US store page. The storecheck tool returned HTTP 404 for ankersolix.com, so this is the rendered page, not the Shopify JSON.

findings.label: Maker's transfer-switch kit for it
findings.value: Home Backup Kit (120V/240V, 30 Amp Cable, 10-Circuit Transfer Switch + Cable, For S5000): Pro/Tran 2 10-circuit 120/240 V manual transfer switch; six 15 A 1-pole, one 20 A 2-pole and one 30 A 2-pole circuits
findings.source_title: Home Backup Kit (120V/240V, 30 Amp Cable, 10-Circuit Transfer Switch + Cable, For S5000)
findings.note: A manual switch, not automatic. Circuit count: 6 + 2 + 2 poles = 10. The price showed 'Price Loading', so none is given. Page copy is inconsistent: one line says the switch 'works flawlessly with Anker SOLIX 2× F3000' while the title and the wattage-meter line name the S5000. No inlet box is listed in the kit.

findings.label: Generator input (maker spec)
findings.value: Anker SOLIX Smart Generator 4,500 W max; third-party generator 4,500 W max; DC generator input 4,500 W max
findings.note: The page does not say which adapter a third-party generator needs. pv magazine reports Anker rates the Smart Generator at 4,300 W into a single S5000.

findings.label: Solar input windows (maker spec)
findings.value: High-PV port 16-165 V, 17 A max, 2,000 W max; Low-PV / Car port 11-60 V, 17 A max, 1,000 W max; 3,000 W in all
findings.note: OffGrid Current already states both voltage ranges; only the 17 A limit per port and the port names are new.

findings.label: AC charging by supply voltage (maker spec)
findings.value: 120 V: 1,800 W max (under 3 hours when current exceeds 12 A); 240 V: 4,500 W max
findings.note: The page does not name the cable needed for 240 V charging.

findings.label: Temperature limits (maker spec)
findings.note: OffGrid Current already states the 32-104°F charging range. Same page: net weight 97 lb, 10.6 × 22.0 × 15.2 in, UL 9540 and UL 9540A certified.

findings.label: Solar connectors and parallel wiring (named reviewer)
findings.value: Andrew Riha (pv magazine USA): the low-voltage input is XT-60i, for one panel or parallel panels; parallel connections 'need a low-voltage solar adapter, such as an MC4 Y-combiner, sold separately'; the high-voltage input is for panels wired in series
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage
findings.note: Published 2026-10-28. Riha measured a 680 W peak from two PS400 panels (800 W rated).

findings.label: E10 Smart Generator cable fit (named reviewer)
findings.value: Andrew Riha (pv magazine USA): 'the E10's Smart Generator cable wouldn't fully seat in the S5000', so he could not test generator charging
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage
findings.note: One reviewer's unit and one cable; Anker's page does not address which Smart Generator cable fits.

findings.label: Alternator charging and 240 V pass-through (named reviewer, citing Anker)
findings.value: Andrew Riha (pv magazine USA): Anker's 800 W Alternator Charger (sold separately) charges through the low-voltage input; per Anker, 'the L14-30R keeps supplying 240 V while the S5000 charges from a 120 V outlet or generator'
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage
findings.note: Riha tested neither. He reports the station feeds a house 'through a transfer switch or inlet box on its L14-30R outlet'.

findings.label: Adapter in the box (named reviewer)
findings.value: Vincent Nguyen (The Gadgeteer): the standalone package includes an AC charging cable and 'a high-voltage solar adapter'
findings.source_title: The Gadgeteer, Anker SOLIX S5000 article by Vincent Nguyen
findings.note: Published 2026-10-29, updated 2026-11-06. Anker's product page showed a 'What's in the Box' heading with no list in my read, so this rests on the reviewer. The page title did not load; source_title is my description.

findings.label: What the cited rival already says on pairings (for the standout check, not maker-verified)
findings.value: OffGrid Current: Jackery 'sells a Smart Transfer Switch made for it' and 'a 240 V manual transfer switch for the Explorer 5000 Plus', with 'up to five Battery Pack 5000 Plus units' to 30,240 Wh; 'Smart Home Panel 10 works with the TITAN 5000 Classic', which 'gives no 240 V output'
findings.note: These are a rival's statements. I could not open Jackery's or EcoFlow's own pages today, so do not publish them as maker-sourced.

unsourced: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus, from the maker: price, stock status, Smart Transfer Switch and manual transfer switch model names, Battery Pack 5000 Plus limit, solar port voltage windows and connectors. jackery.com returned HTTP 429 on three tries and the storecheck tool returned 403. powerstations.reviews lists it at $3,499, sold out, checked Nov 3; I did not use that as a price.

EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Classic, TITAN 5000 and TITAN 5000 Plus, from the maker: price, 120 V-only statement, Smart Home Panel 10 pairing, TITAN 5kWh Extra Battery limit, solar windows. us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429 on three tries and storecheck returned 403. A search summary and reseller Wellbots suggest the extra battery fits all three TITAN models, five per unit; I did not open or verify either.

Pecron F5000LFP: manual figures for solar input voltage and amps, 15 A versus 30 A AC input, FP5000-48V expansion battery limit, and transfer-switch outlet. manuals.plus returned 403 and storecheck returned 403 for pecron.com; only search snippets were seen, so nothing is reported.
OUKITEL ABEARL P5000: no compatibility research done within the tool-call budget.
Anker BP5000 expansion battery US price and the Home Backup Kit for S5000 price: the kit page showed 'Price Loading' and I did not reach a US BP5000 page.
Which adapter or cable a third-party generator needs for the S5000's 4,500 W DC generator input, and which cable or outlet 240 V / 4,500 W AC charging needs: neither Anker page I read says.

A plain-language explanation from Anker of what '120V and 240V outputs cannot be used simultaneously' means when a transfer switch on the L14-30R feeds 120 V circuits: I looked for the S5000 user guide (the page links one under pn=AS510) but did not open it.

Popular Mechanics' S5000 review and Car and Driver's roundup (both cited by ChatGPT): blocked to my fetcher, so I could not check whether either already states the Home Power Panel or simultaneous-output limits.
